bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 2963-byte ASCII witness makes `yara_yyparse` process sequential malformed rules `r01`, `r02`, and `r04` in one parse. In `r01`, the lexer duplicates the 67-character fourth loop identifier `o731entrypointilesizfalseeulfandsizeuletafilesizfalseeulfilesizeule` at `libyara/lexer.l:477`, and `for_variables` stores that pointer in `compiler->loop[3].vars[0].identifier`. A malformed fifth `for` inside the same condition triggers `_FOR_ for_expression error`; its cleanup/decrement leaves slot 3 as a stale deeper slot, and the enclosing `r01` error cleanup at `libyara/grammar.y:1206` then frees that slot once. Because `free_loop_identifiers()` does not null identifiers or reset `vars_count`, `rules error rule` can recover to later malformed rules while slot 3 still names the freed identifier. `r02` only rebuilds shallower loop depths and does not reinitialize slot 3, and `r04` later reaches `compiler->loop_depth == 3` before its own syntax error. The next `_FOR_ for_expression error` at `libyara/grammar.y:1206` therefore frees the same stale slot-3 identifier a second time. AddressSanitizer reports both frees at `grammar.y:1206` and the allocation at `lexer.l:477`. The staged fix makes loop cleanup depth-explicit, nulls freed identifiers, zeros `vars_count`, decrements before normal cleanup, and on error cleans all loop slots once before resetting `compiler->loop_depth = 0`.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the long `r01` fourth loop-variable token into the heap buffer later freed twice.
source.value_from: In the staged `poc`, `rule r01` contains four complete nested `for all <identifier> in (...) : (` prefixes; the fourth identifier `o731entrypointilesizfalseeulfandsizeuletafilesizfalseeulfilesizeule` is visibly 67 characters long, exactly matching the 68-byte ASan allocation after NUL termination.

root_cause.description: During `_FOR_ for_expression error`, `free_loop_identifiers()` always dereferences `compiler->loop[compiler->loop_depth]`. After the malformed fifth `for` in `r01` has already lowered `compiler->loop_depth` from 4 to 3, that expression selects stale slot 3 rather than any active frame, and the helper frees it without clearing `vars_count` or the pointer field.
root_cause.note: The staged patch replaces the macro with `loop_vars_cleanup(loop_depth)`, sets each freed `identifier` to `NULL`, resets `vars_count`, decrements before normal cleanup at lines 1347 and 1441, and on `_FOR_ for_expression error` cleans slots `0..loop_depth` before setting `compiler->loop_depth = 0`.

sink.description: ASan sink. The later `r04` `_FOR_ for_expression error` frees the stale slot-3 identifier pointer a second time.
sink.note: Both the crashing free and the previous free in the saved ASan trace point to `libyara/grammar.y:1206` inside `yara_yyparse`.

tainted_value_origin.description: In `r01`'s fourth nested `for`, the parser stores the heap identifier pointer in `compiler->loop[3].vars[0].identifier`. That slot-owned pointer is the concrete stale state later traversed twice by `free_loop_identifiers()`.

parser_admitted.description: The exact staged 2963-byte witness is installed as the lexer input for one `yyparse` invocation.

next_rule_recovery.code: | rules error rule      /* on error skip until next rule..*/
next_rule_recovery.description: After `YYERROR`, the grammar skips forward to the next `rule` instead of aborting. This is the static mechanism that carries the parse from malformed `r01` into later malformed rules such as `r02` and `r04`.

active_frame_indexing.description: Project code treats only slots below `compiler->loop_depth` as active loop-variable frames; `_yr_compiler_get_var_frame` follows the same `< compiler->loop_depth` rule in `libyara/compiler.c:481-483`. Cleanup at `compiler->loop[compiler->loop_depth]` therefore targets a deeper slot than any active frame.

coarse_trace.summary: In `r01`, the lexer duplicates the long fourth nested loop identifier and `for_variables` stores it in `compiler->loop[3].vars[0].identifier`.
Still inside `r01`, a malformed fifth `for` lowers `compiler->loop_depth` to 3, and the enclosing `_FOR_ for_expression error` then frees stale slot 3 at `grammar.y:1206` without clearing it.
The same `yyparse` invocation recovers with `rules error rule`; malformed `r02` rebuilds only shallower loop depths and leaves slot 3 untouched.

Malformed `r04` later reaches depth 3 and errors before any fourth-loop setup, so `_FOR_ for_expression error` at `grammar.y:1206` frees the stale slot-3 identifier again and ASan reports the double-free.

fine_trace.note: While lexing `rule r01`, the scanner duplicates the fourth complete nested loop variable `o731entrypointilesizfalseeulfandsizeuletafilesizfalseeulfilesizeule`. That visible token is 67 characters long, matching the 68-byte ASan allocation once NUL-terminated.

The `for_variables` action stores that `r01` identifier in `compiler->loop[3].vars[0].identifier`. The witness already contains three earlier complete nested `for all <identifier> in (...) : (` prefixes before this token, so `compiler->loop_depth == 3` at this assignment.
The same `r01` fourth loop reaches its `iterator ':'` action, records its loop address, and increments `compiler->loop_depth` from 3 to 4. From here the active loop frames are slots `0..3`.

`r01` then starts a malformed fifth `for all o731uint16\6`. Its `_FOR_ for_expression error` cleanup runs before any `iterator ':'` action for that fifth loop, so line 1206 operates on slot 4 and line 1207 decrements depth from 4 to 3. Project code only treats slots `< compiler->loop_depth` as active (`parser.c:299-316`, `compiler.c:481-483`), so slot 3 holding step 2's identifier becomes a stale deeper slot.

The enclosing `r01` fourth-loop error reduction now binds `loop_ctx = &compiler->loop[3]` and frees `loop_ctx->vars[0].identifier`, which is the step 1 buffer. Because step 4 already lowered `compiler->loop_depth` to 3, this is wrong-depth cleanup of the stale deeper slot rather than any active frame; it is the first free ASan reports at `grammar.y:1206`.

That same error action decrements depth from 3 to 2, but `free_loop_identifiers()` never nulls identifier fields or resets `vars_count`. Slot 3 therefore keeps `vars_count == 1` and the dangling pointer after the first free.

fine_trace.code: | rules error rule      /* on error skip until next rule..*/
fine_trace.note: The grammar recovers instead of aborting, so the same `yyparse` invocation advances from malformed `r01` to later malformed rules `r02` and `r04` in the saved witness.

The recovered `r02` condition contains only two complete nested `for all <identifier> in (...) : (` prefixes before its malformed third `for`, so parsing that rule raises `compiler->loop_depth` only to 2 before its own errors. No `r02` action reaches slot 3 to reset its stale `vars_count` or identifier.

The later `r04` condition completes three nested `for all <identifier> in (...) : (` prefixes and increments `compiler->loop_depth` back to 3. Its `YSTEM{s` syntax error appears immediately after the third `:(`, before any fourth-loop start action at lines 1290-1294 and 1655 can touch slot 3.

When `r04` hits `_FOR_ for_expression error` at depth 3, the same vulnerable macro again selects `compiler->loop[3]` and frees `loop_ctx->vars[0].identifier`. That second `yr_free` of the step 1 buffer is the ASan crash at `grammar.y:1206`.

allocation_context.note: ASan's allocation stack points to `yr_strdup(yytext)` while lexing an identifier token. In the saved witness, `r01`'s fourth loop identifier `o731entrypointilesizfalseeulfandsizeuletafilesizfalseeulfilesizeule` is 67 characters long and size-matches the reported 68-byte region.

free_context.note: ASan's previous-free stack is identical to the crash stack at the application frames, so the first free also occurs in `_FOR_ for_expression error` at this line.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The 68-byte allocation size matches `r01`'s long fourth loop identifier. The fine trace follows that buffer into slot 3, shows `r01`'s error unwind freeing slot 3 once at `grammar.y:1206`, preserves the stale slot through recovery and `r02`, and reaches a second `grammar.y:1206` free when `r04` errors at depth 3.

poc.trigger: The staged `poc` is the exact 2963-byte ASCII witness that `rules_fuzzer` passes into `yr_lex_parse_rules_string`. Its visible text contains `r01` with four complete nested `for all <identifier> in (...) : (` prefixes followed by malformed `for all o731uint16\6`, then later `r02` with only two complete prefixes before a malformed third `for`, and later `r04` with three complete prefixes followed by `YSTEM{s` immediately after the third `:(`. That exact layout first frees `r01`'s slot-3 identifier during `r01`'s outer error unwind and later frees the same stale slot again when `r04` errors at depth 3.

format.name: ASCII YARA rules text for rules_fuzzer
format.contract: Exactly the staged 2963-byte `poc` file saved in `gt_results/arvo_18902/poc`. The verified trigger is not generalized beyond that witness: it must preserve the witness's specific malformed rule sequence in which `r01` creates the long fourth loop identifier and then errors after a malformed fifth `for`, `r02` recovers without reaching slot 3 again, and `r04` later reaches depth 3 before erroring inside the third loop body.
